parsed.evidence_quote: we have successfully performed DBrASO-based XL-MS analysis of HEK293 cell lysates
In vitro cross-linked cell lysates were digested and fractionated by SEC-HpHt fractionation method.
we have successfully performed DBrASO-based XL-MS analysis of HEK293 cell lysates
designed and synthesized a sulfoxide-containing MS-cleavable haloacetamide-based cross-linker, Dibromoacetamide sulfOxide (DBrASO).
To illustrate the differences between cysteine and lysine cross-linking chemistries, we compared the identified 2297 DBrASO XL-MS proteome with our previously published DSSO XL-proteome
LC-MSn analysis was carried out using an UltiMate 3000 RSLC coupled with an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos mass spectrometer
subsequent MS3 analyses of αA and αT determined the C-C cross-link
remnants of DBrASO following collision-induced dissociation (CID)
The mass tolerances were set as ±20 ppm for parent ions and 0.6 Da for fragment ions.
The mass tolerances were set as ±20 ppm for parent ions and 0.6 Da for fragment ions.
Three biological replicates were performed for each type of XL-MS experiments.

DBrASO cross-linking of HEK293 cell lysates
Three biological replicates were performed for each type of XL-MS experiments.
DBrASO cross-linked proteins were digested by LyC-trypsin as previously described.
cross-linked peptides from HECK 293 cell lysates were first fractionated by a SEC-HpHt method.

A maximum of four variable modifications were also allowed, including cysteine carbamidomethylation, methionine oxidation, N-terminal acetylation, and N-terminal conversion of glutamine to pyroglutamic acid.
This workflow resulted in a total of 12 SEC-HpHt fractions for each proteome-wide XL-MS experiment.

we employed a recently developed two-dimensional fractionation method by coupling peptide size exclusion chromatography (SEC) with tip-based high-pH reverse phase (HpHt) separation (SEC-HpHt) to enrich DBrASO cross-linked peptides from cell lysate digests
